# Send & Retain — for agents

Email automation your agent runs — on your own Resend or SendGrid key.

This repo is the machine-readable surface: an OpenAPI spec, a catalogue of
every MCP tool, and the plugin. The product itself is closed-source and runs
at https://sendandretain.com.

## Two ways in

**MCP** (you are an agent a human is driving) — remote HTTP endpoint:

    https://sendandretain.com/api/mcp

Authorization is **OAuth 2.1**. There is no token to mint or paste: the client
discovers the authorization server from the endpoint and prompts in a browser.
A connected session is always workspace-scoped with write access.

    claude mcp add --transport http sendandretain https://sendandretain.com/api/mcp

Tools are prefixed `email_`. All 92 of them are described in
[`tools.json`](./tools.json) with full JSON Schema for every argument.

**REST** (you are code) — keys are prefixed `aem_` and are a
different credential from MCP, revocable independently. See
[`openapi.json`](./openapi.json).

## The response envelope

Every MCP tool returns `{ ok: true, ... }` or `{ ok: false, error: "..." }`.
Read the error — it is written to say what to do next, not just what failed.

REST uses `{ error: { code, message } }` with the status mapped from the code.

## Scoping

One workspace holds many companies. Because an OAuth session reaches the
whole workspace, company-scoped tools take a `projectId` argument —
enumerate first, then pass it on every call:

    email_list_projects

`tools.json` marks which tools accept it (`acceptsProjectId`).

## Before you change anything

There is **no approval queue** here — a deliberate divergence from
the ads products. Sending is guarded structurally instead:

- Automations are always created **paused**. Enabling one is a separate call
  that requires an explicit `confirm: true`.
- Each company has a `sendsPaused` kill switch and an optional daily send cap,
  both re-checked on the worker path, so they stop already-queued mail too.
- Published template versions are immutable; edits create a new draft.
- Bounces and complaints auto-suppress. **Complaint suppressions can never be
  removed.**
- Delivering mail to a real inbox needs a `write` key **and** the approval
  grant — a separate boolean, not a scope rung. A key refused at the grant
  gets a `403` whose body carries `required_grant`, distinct from
  `required_scope`.

`sendEmail` is single-recipient by design. There is no blast send: broad
delivery happens only through automations a human enabled.

`tools.json` flags every tool that can cause an irreversible or outward-facing
change as `destructive: true` — 58 of 92 here. Treat those as
needing an explicit human instruction, not an inference.
